investigations.title: Locate the disrupted step
investigations.question: Which observations distinguish a production problem from a transport obstruction?
investigations.sourceKind: original schematic observations; not a clinical dataset

variables.holdConstant: same simplified reproductive pathway and observation method

investigations.prediction: Before revealing the observations, predict which two observations would distinguish an obstruction from reduced production.
procedure: Identify testes, tubules, Sertoli cells, interstitial cells, epididymis and duct on the supplied schematic. Record each location and its normal role.
Choose two cases. Keep the observation method fixed and record differences.
Use the table to identify the affected step; propose one additional observation that could reject your explanation.
Read the supplied alternative claim that all low delivery means low production. Explain which case challenges it and revise your claim.
investigations.expected: T has a transport obstruction despite observed germ cells and support. P has altered support/production. S is consistent with reduced upstream signalling. No case establishes an individual fertility diagnosis.
limitations: Schematic observations are not microscopy performance.
Four fictional cases cannot estimate human prevalence or treatment success.
investigations.collaborationEvidence: Independent planning, comparison and revision are observable here. Live teamwork and physical laboratory performance are not certified.

investigations.title: Build and test a cycle explanation
investigations.question: How does the order of four hormone changes support a model of ovulation and endometrial maintenance?
investigations.sourceKind: synthetic relative concentrations on separate hormone scales

variables.holdConstant: one illustrative non-pregnant cycle; each hormone uses its own relative scale

investigations.prediction: Predict which change must precede the LH surge and which hormone would stay raised during a functioning luteal phase.
procedure: Choose labelled axes and plot the four series separately; relative indices do not make hormones equal in molar concentration.
Read the highest estrogen and LH points in time order. Place a provisional ovulation interval, not an exact diagnosis.
Compare day 21 with day 28 and connect the progesterone pattern to endometrial support.
Propose a sampling schedule that could resolve the interval more closely; explain why this model cannot predict a person’s fertile days.
investigations.expected: The highest supplied estrogen point is day 12 and LH is day 14. Progesterone is high at day 21 and lower by day 28. The data are consistent with positive feedback followed by luteal support and withdrawal, but sparse points cannot locate the event exactly.
limitations: An illustrative cycle is not a universal 28-day schedule.
The dataset cannot support personal fertility or contraceptive decisions.
investigations.collaborationEvidence: Independent planning, comparison and revision are observable here. Live teamwork and physical laboratory performance are not certified.

investigations.title: Timing, exposure and developmental evidence
investigations.question: Does an exposure model support the same developmental effect at every stage?
investigations.sourceKind: synthetic non-human cell-model experiment; not human risk estimates

variables.compare: no agent versus agent X at two model stages
variables.observe: number showing marker M out of 40 model samples
variables.holdConstant: agent amount, exposure duration, marker assay, culture conditions

investigations.prediction: Predict how you would distinguish a stage effect from an exposure effect using four groups.
procedure: State the question, comparison groups and one controlled condition before reading results.
Convert all four counts to proportions and compare exposed with unexposed at the same stage.
Connect the early/late contrast to developmental timing; name the evidence needed to connect the marker to organ formation.
Read the alternative claim that the model predicts a precise human risk. Reject or qualify it using organism, endpoint and sample-size limits.
investigations.expected: Early proportions are 0.10 and 0.50, a difference of 0.40; later proportions are 0.125 and 0.225, a difference of 0.10. These synthetic results suggest the marker response depends on stage in this model. They do not quantify risk to a human embryo.
limitations: Marker M is a model endpoint, not a diagnosis or demonstrated birth outcome.
Replication, allocation and uncertainty would be needed in a real experiment.
investigations.collaborationEvidence: Independent planning, comparison and revision are observable here. Live teamwork and physical laboratory performance are not certified.
